key_insight: The paper shows that a change in Hopf topological class in ordered viscoelastic cores cannot occur for free: it must pay one of several finite costs before the sharp-interface limit, and this leads to a transported forced Brakke motion for the core.
engineering_relevance: This gives a mathematically grounded framework for predicting when ordered viscoelastic structures preserve or lose topology, which is useful for modeling complex fluids with defects, vortex tubes, or director reorientation.
method: Derives a projected Ginzburg-Landau-type equation for ordered-core dynamics, separating translation modes from soft, massive, geometric, and collar residuals.
Uses modulated-energy and coercivity arguments to track vortex-tube data on regular intervals and propagate the topological class.
Shows that normalized core measures converge to an integral one-varifold satisfying a transported forced Brakke inequality with an explicit force projection.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports rigorous verification of the structural hypotheses up to the first typed exit time and proves compactness/convergence statements on regular intervals before any limiting Brakke flow is taken.
watch_item: The result depends on several strong structural assumptions and holds only up to the first typed exit time, so robustness outside the ordered-core regime is not guaranteed.
paper_title: Hopf Obstruction and Transported Forced Brakke Motion in Ordered Viscoelastic Cores
